lines.en: Hey, finished for the day yet? I just got my report done.
Wow, that fast? I've still got an email to answer — I can't take it any more!
Don't answer it sloppily — last time you sent it to the wrong client and nearly landed in big trouble.
I know, I'm being really careful this time. Right — done!
Yay! Shall we go for dinner and have a chat?
Sure. Ah Ming says he's coming too — he won't bail again this time, I guess.
You're joking! Last time he said he'd come, and in the end he didn't show.
Where shall we eat? I'm easy, your call.
There's a dai pai dong in Wan Chai — cheap and fantastic, great value.
Last time I went somewhere recommended online and got totally ripped off.
Relax, I've been eating at this one for years — no traps.
Lucky I've got you! Then I'll call Ah Ming too.
Tell him if he bails again this time, I'll really be cross!
Ha ha, OK! See you in a bit!

questions.q: What had A just finished when the conversation starts?
options: A phone call with Ah Ming

questions.q: Why does A warn B not to be sloppy with the email?
options: B once sent one to the wrong client
The boss is checking B's emails
The client is angry with A

questions.q: What can we infer about Ah Ming?
options: He has a habit of not showing up
He recommended the dai pai dong

questions.q: Why is B happy to let A choose the restaurant?
options: A knows the place well and B got burned last time
B has never eaten in Wan Chai
B doesn't like dai pai dongs

units.title: Festivals & Sayings
units.desc: Greet people at New Year and festivals, and use everyday set phrases with the right touch

words.note: THE Lunar New Year greeting. Kids jokingly add 利是逗來 'now hand over the red packet!'

ex.en: Grandma, Happy New Year!

words.note: Works for both January 1st and Lunar New Year, but 恭喜發財 is more typical for Lunar New Year.

ex.en: Happy New Year! All the best this year!

words.note: The go-to wish for elders; also at birthdays.

ex.en: Wishing Grandpa good health!

words.en: may everything go as you wish
words.fr: que tout aille selon vos souhaits
words.note: Pairs with almost any other greeting.

ex.en: Happy New Year, may everything go your way!

words.note: Said to children and students at New Year.

ex.en: Study hard this year — wishing you progress in your studies!

words.note: Married people give 利是 to children and unmarried adults at New Year, weddings and other happy occasions. Use new banknotes, and receive with both hands.

ex.en: How many red packets did you get this year?

words.en: to go round collecting red packets
words.fr: faire la tournée des enveloppes rouges
words.note: What kids (and unmarried adults) do during New Year visits, saying greetings in exchange.

ex.en: The kids love collecting red packets the most at New Year.

words.fr: rendre visite pour le Nouvel An
words.note: Visiting relatives and friends in the first days of New Year, bringing fruit or sweets.

ex.en: On the first day of New Year we go to Grandma's to pay our respects.

words.note: Also written 年三十晚 and said nin4 saa1 aa6 maan5 in fast speech. The family reunion dinner is that night.

ex.en: On New Year's Eve the flower market is packed.

words.fr: repas de réunion du Nouvel An
words.note: The whole family must be there; people travel far to attend.

ex.en: However busy you are, you have to come home for the reunion dinner.

words.note: Many foods are eaten for their 好意頭, e.g. 年糕 = 'higher every year', 髮菜蠔豉 sounds like 發財好市.

ex.en: Eating New Year cake is lucky — it stands for rising higher every year.

words.note: Used to scold or remind: don't argue, don't say unlucky things — it's New Year!

ex.en: It's New Year — don't argue!

words.note: Said right after someone mentions something unlucky (death, illness, failure), to cancel it out. Light-hearted but sincere.

ex.en: Heaven forbid! Don't talk such nonsense.

words.note: 15th day of the 8th lunar month: family dinner, mooncakes, lanterns and moon-gazing.

ex.en: Mid-Autumn Festival is a time for family reunion.

words.note: Classic filling: lotus-seed paste with salted egg yolk (蓮蓉蛋黃).

ex.en: This box of mooncakes was a gift from my colleague.

words.note: Done on the night of Mid-Autumn, often in parks or by the sea.

ex.en: We went to the beach to admire the moon.

words.note: 5th day of the 5th lunar month: dragon-boat races and sticky rice dumplings.

ex.en: Is the Dragon Boat Festival a public holiday?

words.note: Also written 粽. Eaten at Dragon Boat Festival.

ex.en: My mum wraps rice dumplings herself every year.

words.note: For elders add 身體健康 or 長命百歲.

ex.en: Happy birthday! Wishing you good health!

words.en: have a good trip (lit. 'tailwind all the way')
words.note: Some people avoid it for flights (planes take off into the wind) and say 一路平安 instead.

ex.en: Have a good trip, and let us know when you arrive!

words.note: Extremely common for festivals, sales, holidays.

ex.en: At New Year, Victoria Harbour is packed for the fireworks.

words.note: Note the tones: maa1 maa1 fu1 fu1. In casual HK speech 麻麻哋 is also very common.

ex.en: How's your Cantonese? — So-so.

words.note: In fast speech the second 慢 often rises: maan6 maan2 lai4.

ex.en: No rush, take your time, I'll wait for you.

words.en: go for it! you can do it!
words.note: Note the tone change: jau2 (not jau4). Cheering for exams, races, hard times.

ex.en: Exam tomorrow? Go for it!

words.note: A friendly 'how are you', not necessarily an invitation. Answer 食咗喇 or 未啊.

ex.en: Hi there (to an older man), have you eaten?

words.note: Often followed by 你最近點啊?

ex.en: Wow, long time no see! You've lost weight!

sentences.en: When you see elders, remember to wish them a happy new year and good health.
At New Year, married people give red packets to unmarried young people.
On New Year's Eve the whole family eats the reunion dinner together — very lively.
It's New Year — don't say unlucky things!
On Mid-Autumn night we go to the park to admire the moon and eat mooncakes.
At Dragon Boat Festival there are dragon boat races, and lots of people eat rice dumplings.
You're flying to the UK tomorrow? Have a safe trip!
The flower market on New Year's Eve is so packed you can't even move.
Wow, long time no see! How have you been lately?
Have you eaten yet? If not, let's go for dim sum together.
My Cantonese is only so-so — I still need to keep learning.
Exam tomorrow? Go for it, we're all behind you!
Broke a bowl? Never mind — 'it falls and blossoms, bringing wealth and glory'!

grammar.title: Stacking four-character greetings
grammar.explain: Festival wishes are four-character set phrases. String two or three together, and pick one that fits the person: 身體健康 for elders, 學業進步 for students, 生意興隆 for shop owners, 步步高升 for someone with a career. 祝 + person + wish = 'I wish you…'.

examples.en: Happy New Year, and good health!
Wishing you progress in your studies and all the best!
Happy New Year, and may business boom!

grammar.title: Lucky and unlucky words (意頭)
grammar.explain: Hongkongers care about how words sound. 4 sounds like 死 (death), so some avoid the number; if someone says something unlucky, answer 大吉利是; if something breaks at New Year, rescue it with a lucky saying.

examples.en: Some people don't want to live on the 4th floor, because 4 sounds like 'death'.
Heaven forbid! It's New Year, don't talk nonsense!

lines.en: Grandma, Happy New Year! Wishing you good health and all the best!
Good girl! Happy New Year! Here, a red packet for you.
Thank you, Grandma! But I'm thirty already — still getting red packets?
As long as you're not married, you still get one!
Ha ha, then if I never get married, I'll get one every year!
Heaven forbid! It's New Year — don't talk nonsense!
Only joking. I'm still full from last night's reunion dinner — what's good to eat today?
I pan-fried turnip cake and New Year cake — they bring good luck, you know.
Mmm, smells great! Hey, where's my cousin? I haven't seen him for ages.
He's in the UK and couldn't come back this year; he called this morning to wish us a happy New Year.
Oh no! I've broken a bowl!
Never mind — 'it falls and blossoms, bringing wealth and glory'!
Tomorrow night there are fireworks over the harbour. Grandma, do you want to come and watch?
It'll be a sea of people — an old lady like me can't push through. You young ones go.
Then I'll take lots of photos to show you!

questions.q: Why does A still get a red packet at thirty?
Why does Grandma say 大吉利是?
options: A joked about never getting married

questions.q: Why did Grandma make New Year cake?
options: Because there was no turnip cake
It was a gift from a neighbour

questions.q: What can we infer about the cousin?
options: He lives abroad and phoned instead of visiting
He went to see the fireworks

units.title: News & Society
units.desc: Talk about everyday news: rents and salaries, traffic, weather warnings and the environment

words.note: 睇新聞 = watch/read the news. Often san1 man2 in speech.

ex.en: I usually read the news on my phone on the MTR.

words.note: Hongkongers check it for rain and typhoon warnings.

ex.en: The weather forecast says there'll be showers tomorrow afternoon.

words.note: The official weather service; it issues typhoon signals and rain warnings.

ex.en: The Observatory has issued a very hot weather warning.
The government has launched a new recycling scheme.

words.note: Also 'economical'.

ex.en: The economy isn't great lately, and many shops have closed.
Population ageing is a big problem for society.

words.note: The usual word in news reports for 'ordinary people'.

ex.en: Many members of the public think rents are too high.
Hong Kong's public transport is very convenient.

words.note: 塞到一條龍 = jammed solid.

ex.en: There was an accident in the tunnel, and now it's totally jammed.
Property prices are so high, young people can't afford a flat.

words.note: 交租 = pay rent; 加租 = raise the rent.

ex.en: Rent takes up almost half of my salary.

words.note: The biggest hurdle to 買樓.

ex.en: We've been saving for five years and still don't have enough for a down payment.

words.note: Colloquial. 加人工 = pay rise. Formal: 薪金.

ex.en: The company is giving everyone a 3% pay rise this year.
After my dad retires, he wants to move back to his hometown.
Hong Kong people are under a lot of pressure at work.
We should all do our bit to protect the environment.
Air pollution has been quite bad these past few days.

words.note: Short for 環境保護. 好環保 = very green.

ex.en: Bringing your own water bottle when you go out is more eco-friendly.
Remember to put plastic bottles in the recycling bin.
Typhoon signal number 8 is up, which affects many flights.
The number of tourists has increased a lot this year.
We should cut down on plastic bags.
This problem can't be solved in just a day or two.
According to the latest report, rents went up again last month.

words.note: Also tiu4 caa4.

ex.en: A survey found that young people sleep less and less.

sentences.en: Did you see today's news? Rents have gone up again.
The Observatory says there's a typhoon coming this weekend, so better not go out to sea.
The traffic is jammed solid at rush hour — the bus barely moved for half an hour.
Salary rises can't keep up with prices, so life is getting harder and harder.
Many young people still live with their families because they can't afford their own place.
If property prices keep rising, how long will it take to save up a down payment?
The government wants to reduce waste, so it's encouraging people to recycle more.
The latest report shows that the number of people taking the MTR has increased.
A lot of people are worried they won't have enough money after they retire.
Air pollution affects health, especially for the elderly and children.
Is it true that if the black rainstorm signal is up, you don't need to go to work?
With so much work pressure, you should find time to relax.
Parking costs keep going up, so I'd rather take public transport.

grammar.title: Numbers in the news: 成 and 百分之
grammar.explain: Percentages are 百分之 + number (百分之五 = 5%). In speech, tenths are often 成: 一成 = 10%, 兩成 = 20%, 三成半 = 35%.

examples.en: Rent takes up 40% of his salary.

grammar.title: Reporting what you heard: 話 / 聽講 / 根據
grammar.explain: To pass on news: X 話… (X says…), 聽講… (I heard that…), 根據… (according to…, more formal). Add 喎 wo3 at the end to signal 'that's what they say'.

examples.en: The Observatory says it'll be 34 degrees tomorrow.
I heard the MTR is raising fares again next month.
According to the survey, most people want shorter working hours.

lines.en: Have you seen this news item? It says rents rose again last month.
No wonder my landlord just told me he's raising the rent by two thousand dollars.
Two thousand? That's a lot! Your salary hasn't gone up that much.
Exactly. Rent already takes up almost half my salary — the pressure's huge.
Have you thought about moving to the New Territories? Rents there are a bit cheaper.
I have, but the traffic's a problem — the commute would be over an hour.
And at rush hour, if there's a jam, you could be late all the time.
Right. If you add in the extra transport costs, it might not save much.
There's also a survey in the news saying many young people want to move out, but can't afford to.
No surprise. With property prices this high, the down payment alone takes years of saving.
Has the government said how it'll solve it?
The report says they'll build more public housing, but it'll take a few years.
Then what will you do? Renew the lease or move?
I'll stay for now and save money — I'll think again when I'm better off.

questions.q: What news did A read?
options: Rents went up again last month

questions.q: Why is B worried about the rent?
options: The landlord is raising it by $2,000
B wants to buy a flat next month
The flat is too far from work

questions.q: Why might moving to the New Territories not help B much?
options: Longer commutes and extra transport costs

questions.q: What does B decide to do for now?
options: Buy a flat with a friend
